A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ProxyCoT study. Their text, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–B are readable and support comparison; appendix content is preserved despite reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original training and evaluation results on SciTrek, HotpotQA and Loong, including baseline comparisons, training-stage ablations and alternative-proxy experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds a controlled-noise experiment on SciTrek and HotpotQA in Table 10.

M1.justification: The two-stage ProxyCoT-ZS and ProxyCoT-RL procedures, teacher/student checkpoint choices, objectives and reward remain unchanged. Section 3.2 corrects M_S to M_init without changing the previously described procedure; Figure 2 redraws the same pipeline.

E1.justification: SciTrek, HotpotQA and the English financial/academic Loong coverage remain unchanged. Section 6.2 adds a controlled input condition: proxies retaining oracle evidence while including injected irrelevant sentences, extending the existing oracle, retrieved and random-only proxy scenarios.

E2.justification: The zero-shot models, full-context SFT/RLVR/CoT-distillation baselines and Loong comparators remain unchanged in the corresponding comparisons. The new RAG discussion interprets existing proxy scores; it introduces no evaluated RAG baseline.

E3.justification: Table 10 introduces noisy-proxy training for Qwen3-4B-Instruct with oracle:noise sentence ratios of 1:0, 1:1, 1:2 and 1:5. Existing splits, budgets, metrics and decoding settings are retained. The new experiment does not clearly specify whether evaluation uses proxy or full contexts.

E4.justification: v1 already examines training-stage removal and alternative proxy construction in Tables 8–9. v2 retains these analyses and adds a focused sensitivity study testing the effect of increasing irrelevant-sentence noise on both datasets in Table 10.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without experimental seed information, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. Table 10 follows the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results in Tables 4–9 are unchanged. Table 10 adds SciTrek exact-match scores of 91.3, 89.9 and 85.3, and HotpotQA accuracy scores of 90.1, 88.4 and 83.7, at noise ratios 1:1, 1:2 and 1:5 respectively. These are additional experimental conditions, not revised main-benchmark performance.

T1.justification: The proxy-context definition, reasoning distributions, SFT losses in Equations 1–2 and reward in Equation 3 are retained. No substantive mathematical assumption, derivation or proof changes; the new RAG upper-bound statement is a prose interpretation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about the proxy/full-context gap, two-stage training, performance and inference efficiency, and out-of-domain generalization.

C2.justification: Section 5 newly interprets proxy-context performance as an upper bound for RAG with perfect retrieval. Section 6.2 adds the interpretation that ProxyCoT-RL remains robust to injected noise with marginal degradation. Existing proxy-quality explanations and the limitations section remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents random irrelevant-sentence augmentation, sentence-count ratios and resulting proxy lengths for the noise experiment. Existing implementation settings, hardware, resource-access information, HotpotQA construction procedure and judge prompt are retained.

R1.justification: Section 5 newly positions the existing proxy-context evaluations as an oracle-retrieval ceiling for RAG approaches. The cited works and substantive coverage of the Related Work section otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Limited editing corrects RVLR to RLVR and inconsistent model notation, adds author contact details and acknowledgments, and inserts the RAG and noise discussions. The main section ordering and narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn, Table 10 is added, Table 9 headers are refined and existing tables shift positions. Appendices A–B change to full-width layout; the unchanged judge prompt moves from numbered Figure 3 on one page to an unnumbered box spanning two pages.

improvement.justification: Table 10 adds useful controlled-noise evidence to v1's proxy-quality analysis while preserving the original experiments, and terminology corrections improve consistency. The gain is limited: Table 10 leaves the evaluated context unclear, and the new claim of an upper bound for any RAG approach exceeds the comparisons shown.
